turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, I'm Dr.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Haddad.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Can you confirm your full name and date of birth for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thomas Kowalsik, May 3rd, 1981. Thanks, Thomas.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You're walking a little carefully there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: What happened? Yes, Saturday I was helping move pallets at work, and I picked up a box of floor tile wrong. Twisted, you know, felt something grab in my lower back, right side.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Ouch, where do you work again? Harbor point distribution,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I'm a shift laid in the warehouse.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Got it, on a scale of zero to ten, how bad is the pain?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Right now, maybe a six. When I bend over to tie my shoes, it's like an eight.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Does it go anywhere,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: like down your leg? A little into the right butt cheek, not down the leg.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any numbness or tingling in your legs or feet. Any weakness, like your foot dragging.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, no numbness,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: legs feel normal just the back. I have to ask a few important ones. Any numbness in the grind or between your legs, like where you'd sit on a saddle.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any trouble controlling your bladder or bowels or trouble starting to pee.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No, everything's working fine there.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any fevers, unexplained weight loss, or any history of cancer.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: None of that. Have you had back trouble before? I had sciatica on the left side maybe six years ago, did physical therapy, and it went away completely, haven't had it since.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Good, what have you tried so far?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ibuprofen, two of the two hundreds a couple times a day, and my wife Agnieszka's heating pad. The heat helps some. I'm kind of worried, though. A guy on my crew herniated a disc, doing the same thing, and needed surgery. That's understandable.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Let's take a look. Blood pressure is 134 over 84, pulse 76, temperature 98 .4. Can you stand and bend forward for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's about as far as I go.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Okay, forward bending is limited by pain,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: about halfway.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I can feel tight, tender muscles along the right side of your lower back. No tenderness when I press right on the spine itself.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Now lie back.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I'm going to raise each leg straight. Just pulls in the back a little. Straight leg raise is negative on both sides. Strength is normal in both legs, reflexes are equal at the knees and ankles, and you can feel my touch the same on both sides. You walked in normally, and you can walk on your heels and toes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: So, is it a disc?

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: I don't think so. This looks like a strain of the muscles in your lower back. There are no warning signs, so you don't need an x -ray or MRI right now. Most of these get a lot better in two to four weeks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, that's a relief. For pain,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: take ibuprofen 600 mg three times a day with food for the next week or so. I'm also prescribing cyclobenzaprine, a muscle relaxer, 5 mg at bedtime as needed for spasm. It can make you drowsy, so no driving or running the forklift after you take it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Garted only at night.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Keep using heat and keep moving. gentle walking is better than bed rest I'll write you a note for light duty no lifting over 20 pounds through October 15th my supervisor will want that thanks if you're not better in two weeks come back and we'll start physical therapy and if you ever lose control of your bladder or bowels get numb between your legs or a leg gets weak go to the emergency room right away okay Hopefully, it doesn't come to that I don't expect it to let's plan a follow -up in two weeks. Take care of that back Thomas
